bartolomeo-scappi.name: Bartolomeo Scappi
bartolomeo-scappi.summary: Italian Renaissance chef and food writer (c. 1500–1577), famous for his high-profile clients, including as personal chef to Pope Pius IV.

pope-pius-iv.name: Pope Pius IV
pope-pius-iv.summary: Head of the Catholic Church and Papal States from 1559 to 1565, who presided over the final session of the Council of Trent and improved Rome's water supply.

cristoforo-di-messisbugo.name: Cristoforo di Messisbugo
cristoforo-di-messisbugo.summary: A steward of the House of Este in Ferrara and an Italian Renaissance cook, active until his death in 1548.

ippolito-ii-d-este.name: Ippolito II d'Este
ippolito-ii-d-este.summary: Italian cardinal and statesman (1509–1572) of the House of Este, who stripped Hadrian's Villa of marbles and statues to decorate his own Villa d'Este.

house-of-gonzaga.name: Gonzaga family
house-of-gonzaga.summary: An Italian princely family that ruled Mantua in northern Italy from 1328 to 1708, also holding Monferrato and Nevers, and producing two Holy Roman empresses.

francesco-leonardi-chef.name: Francesco Leonardi
francesco-leonardi-chef.summary: Italian chef and food author active in the 18th century who ended his career cooking for Empress Catherine II of Russia; his cookbook sketched a history of Italian cuisine, and he is credited as the first chef to regularly use tomatoes.

antoine-augustin-parmentier.name: Antoine-Augustin Parmentier
antoine-augustin-parmentier.summary: French pharmacist and agronomist (1737–1813) who successfully promoted the potato as a food source, established France's first mandatory smallpox vaccination campaign, and pioneered extracting sugar from sugar beets.

pappa-al-pomodoro.name: Pappa al pomodoro
pappa-al-pomodoro.summary: A thick Tuscan bread soup made from tomatoes, stale bread, olive oil, garlic and basil, originally devised by tenant farmers to use up scarce tomatoes and leftover bread.

sfogliatella.name: Sfogliatella Santa Rosa
sfogliatella.summary: The 17th-century ancestor of today's sfogliatella pastry, created in the monastery of Santa Rosa in Conca dei Marini, Campania.

conca-dei-marini.name: Conca dei Marini
conca-dei-marini.summary: A small coastal town in the Salerno province of Campania, Italy, once a trading base of the Republic of Amalfi and later sacked by Turkish pirates in 1543.

humorism.name: Four Humors
humorism.summary: An ancient system of medicine, used by Greek and Roman physicians, holding that the body's workings depended on a balance of the four humors; it fell out of favor in the 17th century.

leonardo-da-vinci.name: Leonardo da Vinci
leonardo-da-vinci.summary: An Italian polymath of the High Renaissance (1452–1519) — painter, engineer, scientist and theorist whose notebooks covered anatomy, astronomy and botany — regarded as epitomizing Renaissance genius alongside his contemporary Michelangelo.

michelangelo.name: Michelangelo
michelangelo.summary: Italian sculptor, painter, architect and poet of the High Renaissance (1475–1564), famed for the Pietà, David, and the Sistine Chapel ceiling and Last Judgment frescoes.

raphael.name: Raphael
raphael.summary: Italian painter and architect (1483–1520) of the High Renaissance, ranked with Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo as one of the era's three great masters.

antonello-da-messina.name: Antonello da Messina
antonello-da-messina.summary: Italian Early Renaissance painter (c. 1425–1479) from Messina whose work, shaped by Early Netherlandish influences, in turn influenced painters in northern Italy, especially Venice.

mannerism.name: Mannerism
mannerism.summary: A European art style emerging after the Italian High Renaissance around 1520, exaggerating proportion and balance into tension and elegance; it lasted into the late 16th century in Italy.

palladian-architecture.name: Palladianism
palladian-architecture.summary: A European architectural style based on the 16th-century work of Andrea Palladio, developed in England from the early 17th century and later revived after a reaction against Baroque design.

david-michelangelo.name: David (Michelangelo)
david-michelangelo.summary: A marble statue carved by Michelangelo between 1501 and 1504, the first colossal marble sculpture since classical antiquity, unveiled in Florence and later moved to the Galleria dell'Accademia.

andrea-palladio.name: Andrea Palladio
andrea-palladio.summary: An Italian Renaissance architect (1508–1580) influenced by Roman and Greek design, best known for villas and country houses; his treatise shaped later architecture.

villa-la-rotonda.name: Villa Capra "La Rotonda"
villa-la-rotonda.summary: A Renaissance villa near Vicenza, Italy, designed by Andrea Palladio and begun in 1567, whose form later inspired countless Neoclassical buildings across Europe.

giovanni-paolo-panini.name: Giovanni Paolo Panini
giovanni-paolo-panini.summary: Italian Baroque painter and architect (1691–1765) known as a "view painter" of Rome, especially its ancient ruins, including a famous view of the Pantheon's interior.

tienne-fran-ois-de-choiseul-duke-of-choi.name: Étienne François de Choiseul
tienne-fran-ois-de-choiseul-duke-of-choi.summary: French army officer, diplomat and statesman (1719–1785) who served as Foreign Minister of France and is closely associated with France's defeat in the Seven Years' War.
tienne-fran-ois-de-choiseul-duke-of-choi.source_title: Étienne François de Choiseul, Duke of Choiseul

laoco-n-and-his-sons.name: Laocoön and His Sons
laoco-n-and-his-sons.summary: An ancient marble sculpture depicting the Trojan priest Laocoön and his sons attacked by sea serpents, excavated in Rome in 1506 and long displayed in the Vatican Museums.

apollo-belvedere.name: Apollo Belvedere
apollo-belvedere.summary: A celebrated 2nd-century AD marble sculpture, likely a Roman copy of a 4th-century BC bronze, long regarded as the pinnacle of ancient art after its Renaissance rediscovery.

piazza-navona.name: Piazza Navona
piazza-navona.summary: A public square in Rome built on the site of the ancient Stadium of Domitian, transformed in the 17th century into a showcase of Baroque design by Bernini and Borromini.

piazza-di-spagna.name: Piazza di Spagna
piazza-di-spagna.summary: A square in central Rome at the foot of the Spanish Steps, named for the Palazzo di Spagna, seat of the Spanish embassy to the Holy See.

nicola-salvi.name: Nicola Salvi
nicola-salvi.summary: Italian architect (1697–1751) best known for designing Rome's Trevi Fountain.

herculaneum.name: Herculaneum
herculaneum.summary: Ancient Roman town near Naples buried by the 79 AD eruption of Mount Vesuvius, whose volcanic material preserved even wooden objects and food.

japanning.name: Japanning
japanning.summary: A European imitation of East Asian lacquerwork originating in the 17th century, usually a heavy black glossy finish, though also made in red, green or blue.

treaty-of-cateau-cambr-sis.name: Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis
treaty-of-cateau-cambr-sis.summary: Ended the Italian Wars in 1559 through two linked treaties; France abandoned claims to Naples, Sicily and Milan, restored Savoy's independence, and recognized Elizabeth I as England's queen.

kingdom-of-naples.name: Kingdom of Naples
kingdom-of-naples.summary: A state ruling southern Italy from 1282 to 1816, formed after the War of the Sicilian Vespers and later contested by France and Spain before coming under Spanish control by 1504.

kingdom-of-sicily.name: Kingdom of Sicily
kingdom-of-sicily.summary: A state ruling Sicily and southern Italy from 1130, founded by Roger II; after the 1282 Sicilian Vespers revolt it became a separate island kingdom later tied to the Crown of Aragon and Spain.

charles-v-holy-roman-emperor.name: Charles V
charles-v-holy-roman-emperor.summary: Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain (1500–1558) whose Habsburg realms in Europe and the Americas were together called 'the empire on which the sun never sets'.

italian-war-of-1521-1526.name: Italian War of 1521-1526
italian-war-of-1521-1526.summary: A conflict from 1521 to 1526 pitting France and Venice against Holy Roman Emperor Charles V, Henry VIII of England, and the Papal States, part of the broader Italian Wars.

pope-clement-vii.name: Pope Clement VII
pope-clement-vii.summary: Born Giulio de' Medici, head of the Catholic Church from 1523 to 1534; his reign was marked by the Protestant Reformation and rivalry between Charles V and Francis I.

castel-sant-angelo.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
castel-sant-angelo.summary: A towering rotunda in Rome originally built as Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum, later used by popes as a fortress and now a museum; it was once the city's tallest building.

swiss-guard.name: Swiss Guard
swiss-guard.summary: The Vatican's ceremonial guard force, established in 1506 to protect the Pope, known for its Renaissance-style uniform and, since 1981, greater emphasis on modern security training.

francis-i-of-france.name: Francis I of France
francis-i-of-france.summary: King of France from 1515 until his death in 1547, a major patron of the arts who brought Italian artists such as Leonardo da Vinci to France and promoted the French Renaissance.

treaty-of-cambrai.name: Treaty of Cambrai
treaty-of-cambrai.summary: Known as the 'Peace of the Ladies,' it confirmed Habsburg dominance over Milan and Naples and renewed the 1526 Treaty of Madrid, resolving disputes over the Burgundian inheritance.

louise-of-savoy.name: Louise of Savoy
louise-of-savoy.summary: French noblewoman (1476–1531), mother of King Francis I, who served three times as regent of France during her son's absence.

margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy.name: Margaret of Austria
margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy.summary: Habsburg archduchess (1480-1530) who served as governor of the Habsburg Netherlands from 1507 to 1515 and again from 1519 until her death in 1530, for her father Maximilian I and later her nephew Charles V.
margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy.source_title: Margaret of Austria, Duchess of Savoy

odet-de-foix-viscount-of-lautrec.name: Odet de Foix
odet-de-foix-viscount-of-lautrec.summary: French military leader and Marshal of France (1485–1528) who commanded League forces during the Italian Wars and died of typhus while campaigning to conquer Naples.
odet-de-foix-viscount-of-lautrec.source_title: Odet de Foix, Viscount of Lautrec

benvenuto-cellini.name: Benvenuto Cellini
benvenuto-cellini.summary: Italian goldsmith, sculptor and author (1500–1571) known for works including the Perseus statue and an autobiography considered a major 16th-century document.

treaty-of-barcelona-1529.name: Treaty of Barcelona (1529)
treaty-of-barcelona-1529.summary: A 1529 alliance between Emperor Charles V and Pope Clement VII aiming to bring peace to Italy and resist Ottoman advances; Charles agreed to restore the Medici to Florence.

cosimo-i-de-medici.name: Cosimo I de' Medici
cosimo-i-de-medici.summary: Second and last duke of Florence (1537-1569) and later first grand duke of Tuscany, who conquered Siena and built the Uffizi and Boboli Gardens.

battle-of-marciano.name: Battle of Marciano
battle-of-marciano.summary: A 1554 battle near Arezzo, Tuscany, where Florentine-Imperial forces crushed the Republic of Siena and France's army, leading to Siena's absorption into Florence.

siena.name: Siena
siena.summary: A historic city in Tuscany, Italy, once a major medieval banking center famous for its Renaissance art, medieval cityscape, and the Palio horse race.

grand-duchy-of-tuscany.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
grand-duchy-of-tuscany.summary: An Italian monarchy centered on Florence that existed from 1569 to 1860, ruled first by the Medici after Cosimo I was made grand duke by the pope.

catherine-de-medici.name: Catherine de' Medici
catherine-de-medici.summary: Queen of France from 1547 to 1559 through marriage to Henry II, and mother of three French kings whose reigns she strongly influenced.

miguel-de-cervantes.name: Miguel de Cervantes
miguel-de-cervantes.summary: A Spanish writer (1547–1616) regarded as the greatest in the Spanish language, best known for Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel.

le-morte-d-arthur.name: Le Morte d'Arthur
le-morte-d-arthur.summary: A 15th-century Middle English prose compilation of Arthurian legends by Sir Thomas Malory, completed around 1470 and first printed in 1485.

giovanni-francesco-straparola.name: Giovanni Francesco Straparola
giovanni-francesco-straparola.summary: Italian writer (c. 1485–1558) whose story collection The Facetious Nights includes some of the earliest known printed fairy tales in Europe.

giambattista-basile.name: Giambattista Basile
giambattista-basile.summary: Italian poet and courtier (1566 to 1632) whose posthumously published Pentamerone contains some of the oldest recorded European fairy tales.

pentamerone.name: Pentamerone
pentamerone.summary: A collection of Neapolitan fairy tales by Giambattista Basile, published in 1634 and among the earliest printed fairy tale collections in Europe.

niccol-machiavelli.name: Niccolò Machiavelli
niccol-machiavelli.summary: Florentine diplomat, author, philosopher and historian (1469–1527) of the Italian Renaissance, best known for The Prince and often called the father of modern political philosophy.

the-prince.name: The Prince
the-prince.summary: 16th-century political treatise by Niccolò Machiavelli written as a guide for new princes, arguing immoral acts are sometimes necessary to achieve political glory.

thomas-more.name: Thomas More
thomas-more.summary: An English lawyer, statesman and Renaissance humanist (1478–1535) who wrote Utopia and was executed for refusing to accept Henry VIII's break with the Catholic Church.

utopia-book.name: Utopia
utopia-book.summary: A 1516 work of fiction and political satire by Thomas More, written in Latin, depicting a fictional island society's customs.

pedro-calder-n-de-la-barca.name: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
pedro-calder-n-de-la-barca.summary: Spanish dramatist and poet (1600–1681) of the Spanish Golden Age, often called 'the Spanish Shakespeare' for his many verse dramas and mystery plays.

lope-de-vega.name: Lope de Vega
lope-de-vega.summary: A Spanish playwright and poet (1562–1635) of the Spanish Golden Age, considered second only to Cervantes, who wrote around 500 plays and 3,000 sonnets.

william-shakespeare.name: William Shakespeare
william-shakespeare.summary: English playwright, poet and actor (c. 1564–1616), widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language, known for about 39 plays and 154 sonnets.

moli-re.name: Molière
moli-re.summary: French playwright, actor and poet (1622–1673) regarded as one of the greatest writers in the French language, whose comedies are still widely performed today.

giovanni-boccaccio.name: Giovanni Boccaccio
giovanni-boccaccio.summary: Italian writer and poet (1313–1375), correspondent of Petrarch, best known for The Decameron, a collection of short stories that shaped the Italian literary tradition.

cleopatra.name: Cleopatra
cleopatra.summary: Last active Hellenistic pharaoh, ruling Ptolemaic Egypt from 51 to 30 BC; her death marked Egypt becoming a Roman province and the end of the Hellenistic period.

commedia-dell-arte.name: Commedia dell'arte
commedia-dell-arte.summary: An early form of professional theatre from Italy, popular across Europe from the 16th to 18th centuries, known for masked stock characters and improvised comic performances.

francesco-guicciardini.name: Francesco Guicciardini
francesco-guicciardini.summary: Italian historian and statesman (1483–1540), friend and critic of Machiavelli and one of the major political writers of the Renaissance; his History of Italy pioneered a realistic style of history using government sources.

pietro-bembo.name: Pietro Bembo
pietro-bembo.summary: Venetian scholar, poet and cardinal (1470–1547) whose writing shaped the Tuscan dialect into the literary language that became modern Italian.

pontifical-academy-of-arcadia.name: Academy of Arcadia
pontifical-academy-of-arcadia.summary: An Italian literary academy founded in Rome in 1690 to reform poetry by returning to classical simplicity against ornate Baroque style; it admitted women and grew to over 1,300 members.

alberto-asor-rosa.name: Alberto Asor Rosa
alberto-asor-rosa.summary: Italian literary critic, historian and politician (1933–2022) who served in Italy's Chamber of Deputies and edited leftist cultural magazines.

christina-queen-of-sweden.name: Christina, Queen of Sweden
christina-queen-of-sweden.summary: Queen of Sweden from 1632 until her abdication in 1654, remembered as one of the era's most erudite women; she converted to Catholicism and settled in Rome.

san-pietro-in-montorio.name: San Pietro in Montorio
san-pietro-in-montorio.summary: Church in Rome whose courtyard contains Bramante's Tempietto, a small commemorative shrine.

giovanni-paolo-marana.name: Giovanni Paolo Marana
giovanni-paolo-marana.summary: Genoese writer of fiction and non-fiction (1642–1693), remembered for his conviction over failing to reveal a conspiracy to cede Savona to Savoy.

montesquieu.name: Montesquieu
montesquieu.summary: French political philosopher (1689 to 1755) known for developing the theory of separation of powers and for his 1748 book The Spirit of Law, which influenced the US Constitution.

persian-letters.name: Persian Letters
persian-letters.summary: A 1721 satirical novel by Montesquieu describing two fictional Persian noblemen's experiences in France under Louis XIV, criticising French society through their outsider eyes.

daniel-defoe.name: Daniel Defoe
daniel-defoe.summary: English writer, journalist and spy (c. 1660–1731), best known for the novel Robinson Crusoe (1719), an early figure in the English novel.

girolamo-brusoni.name: Girolamo Brusoni
girolamo-brusoni.summary: An Italian Baroque writer (1614–after 1686) and former Carthusian monk who fled his order and was later imprisoned.

pace-pasini.name: Pace Pasini
pace-pasini.summary: Italian marinist poet and novelist (1583–1644), best known for the Baroque novel L'historia del cavalier perduto.

alessandro-manzoni.name: Alessandro Manzoni
alessandro-manzoni.summary: An Italian philosopher, poet and novelist (1785-1873) best known for The Betrothed (1827), a milestone that helped unify the modern Italian language and symbolized Italy's unification movement.

the-betrothed.name: The Betrothed
the-betrothed.summary: An Italian historical novel by Alessandro Manzoni, published in its final form in 1840–1842 and often called the most widely read novel in Italian, noted for its depiction of the 1629–1631 Milan plague.

galileo-galilei.name: Galileo Galilei
galileo-galilei.summary: An Italian astronomer, physicist, and polymath (1564–1642) called the father of observational astronomy and modern science, whose telescope discoveries and support for heliocentrism led to conflict with the Catholic Church.

caravel.name: Caravel
caravel.summary: A small, fast sailing ship developed from Iberian fishing boats, used by Portuguese and Spanish explorers during the 15th- and 16th-century Age of Exploration.

giordano-bruno.name: Giordano Bruno
giordano-bruno.summary: Italian friar and philosopher who argued the stars were distant suns with their own planets and that the universe is infinite; burned at the stake in 1600 for heresy.

campo-de-fiori.name: Campo de' Fiori
campo-de-fiori.summary: A rectangular square in Rome near Piazza Navona, named 'Field of Flowers' after its origin as a medieval meadow.

roger-joseph-boscovich.name: Roger Joseph Boscovich
roger-joseph-boscovich.summary: Physicist, astronomer and Jesuit priest (1711–1787) from Ragusa who produced an early precursor of atomic theory and discovered in 1753 that the Moon has no atmosphere.

christopher-maire.name: Christopher Maire
christopher-maire.summary: English Jesuit and writer on astronomy (1697–1767).

papal-states.name: Papal States
papal-states.summary: The official name of the Papal States, territories on the Italian Peninsula ruled directly by the pope from 756 to 1870, established when the Frankish king Pepin the Short granted lands to Pope Stephen II.

john-cabot.name: John Cabot
john-cabot.summary: Italian navigator (c. 1450–c. 1499) whose 1497 voyage to North America under England's Henry VII is the earliest known European exploration of the coast since the Norse visits.

giovanni-da-verrazzano.name: Giovanni da Verrazzano
giovanni-da-verrazzano.summary: An Italian explorer (1491–1528) who, serving King Francis I of France, became the first European to explore North America's Atlantic coast from Florida to New Brunswick, in 1524.

christopher-columbus.name: Christopher Columbus
christopher-columbus.summary: Italian explorer and navigator (1451–1506) whose four Spanish-sponsored voyages opened the way for European exploration and colonization of the Americas.

house-of-medici.name: Medici family
house-of-medici.summary: An Italian banking family that rose to rule Florence and later the Grand Duchy of Tuscany, producing four popes and two queens of France between the 15th and 17th centuries.

house-of-farnese.name: Farnese family
house-of-farnese.summary: An influential Renaissance Italian family holding titles including Duke of Parma and Piacenza, whose members included Pope Paul III and a governor of the Spanish Netherlands.

house-of-este.name: House of Este
house-of-este.summary: A European dynasty of Lombard origin whose younger branch ruled Ferrara, Modena and Reggio from the 13th to 19th centuries, while its elder branch produced Britain's Hanoverian monarchs.

house-of-savoy.name: House of Savoy
house-of-savoy.summary: A royal dynasty established in 1003 that expanded from the Alpine County of Savoy to rule Sicily, Sardinia and eventually the unified Kingdom of Italy until 1946.

duchy-of-milan.name: Duchy of Milan
duchy-of-milan.summary: A Northern Italian state created in 1395 by Gian Galeazzo Visconti, later prospering under the Sforza family's silk industry before falling to Napoleon's forces in 1796.

ferdinand-i-holy-roman-emperor.name: Ferdinand I, Holy Roman Emperor
ferdinand-i-holy-roman-emperor.summary: Holy Roman Emperor from 1556, also King of Bohemia, Hungary and Croatia and Archduke of Austria, who governed Habsburg lands for his brother Charles V before succeeding him and facing Ottoman advances and the Reformation.

philip-ii-of-spain.name: Philip II of Spain
philip-ii-of-spain.summary: King of Spain from 1556 and Portugal from 1580, under whom Spain reached its height of power, including the conquest of the Philippines, named in his honor.

southern-italy.name: Mezzogiorno
southern-italy.summary: Term for southern Italy, historically the lands of the former Kingdoms of Naples and Sicily, later united as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

charles-iii-of-spain.name: Charles III of Spain
charles-iii-of-spain.summary: Fourth son of Philip V of Spain who became Duke of Parma and Piacenza in 1731, then led Spanish troops to seize Naples and Sicily in 1734–35, ruling there before later becoming King of Spain.

bernardo-tanucci.name: Bernardo Tanucci
bernardo-tanucci.summary: Italian jurist and statesman (1698-1783) who brought an enlightened absolutism style of government to the Kingdom of Naples under Charles III and his son Ferdinand IV.

ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.name: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.summary: King of Naples and Sicily, later the Two Sicilies, from 1759 until 1825; deposed twice, by a revolutionary republic in 1799 and by French invasion in 1806, before being restored in 1815.
ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.source_title: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies

iberian-union.name: Iberian Union
iberian-union.summary: The 1580–1640 personal union under Spain's Habsburg kings joining the crowns of Portugal, Castile and Aragon, ended when Portugal's Braganza dynasty broke away.

spanish-golden-age.name: Spanish Golden Age
spanish-golden-age.summary: A period of intense Spanish artistic, literary and intellectual flourishing, roughly 1492 to 1659 politically, coinciding with Spain's rise as a leading power under the Habsburgs.

maria-carolina-of-austria.name: Maria Carolina
maria-carolina-of-austria.summary: Queen of Naples and Sicily as wife of King Ferdinand IV, and de facto ruler of the kingdom; she pushed Enlightenment reforms before making Naples a police state to block French revolutionary ideas.

sir-john-acton-6th-baronet.name: Sir John Acton
sir-john-acton-6th-baronet.summary: A British naval officer and politician (1736–1811) who served in the Tuscan and Neapolitan navies and as Prime Minister of Naples and Sicily under Ferdinand IV.

house-of-bourbon.name: House of Bourbon
house-of-bourbon.summary: A dynasty descended from the Capetians that ruled France and Navarre from 1589 and later gained the thrones of Spain, Naples, Sicily and Parma; Spain and Luxembourg still have Bourbon monarchs today.

palaeologus-montferrat.name: Palaeologus-Montferrat family
palaeologus-montferrat.summary: An Italian noble family descended from a Byzantine prince who inherited the March of Montferrat in 1306, giving it a claim to the Byzantine imperial legacy.

vincenzo-ii-gonzaga.name: Vincenzo II Gonzaga
vincenzo-ii-gonzaga.summary: Duke of Mantua and Duke of Montferrat from 1626 until his death in 1627; he briefly held a cardinalate before marrying and died without children.

charles-i-gonzaga.name: Charles I Gonzaga
charles-i-gonzaga.summary: Duke of Mantua and Montferrat from 1627 to 1637, also known as Charles III as Duke of Nevers and Rethel and Prince of Arche and Charleville.

andreas-palaiologos.name: Andreas Palaiologos
andreas-palaiologos.summary: Eldest son of Thomas Palaiologos, Despot of the Morea, and nephew of the last Byzantine emperor, Constantine XI; he claimed the title Emperor of Constantinople from 1483 until his death in 1502.

ferdinand-ii-of-aragon.name: Ferdinand II of Aragon
ferdinand-ii-of-aragon.summary: King of Aragon from 1479 and, through marriage to Isabella I, joint ruler of Castile as one of the Catholic Monarchs; together they sponsored Columbus's 1492 voyage and completed the Reconquista by conquering Granada.

isabella-i-of-castile.name: Isabella I of Castile
isabella-i-of-castile.summary: Queen of Castile and León from 1474 to 1504 and, with her husband Ferdinand II of Aragon, one of the Catholic Monarchs who completed the Reconquista and financed Columbus's 1492 voyage.

nicolaus-copernicus.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
nicolaus-copernicus.summary: Renaissance polymath (1473–1543) who proposed that the Sun, not Earth, is at the center of the universe, triggering the Copernican Revolution.

de-revolutionibus-orbium-coelestium.name: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium
de-revolutionibus-orbium-coelestium.summary: Nicolaus Copernicus's 1543 book proposing that the Earth and planets orbit the Sun, challenging the long-accepted Earth-centered model of Ptolemy.

pope-paul-iii.name: Pope Paul III
pope-paul-iii.summary: Head of the Catholic Church and Papal States from 1534 to 1549, who launched the Catholic Reformation with the Council of Trent and recognized new orders including the Jesuits.

alessandro-farnese-cardinal.name: Alessandro Farnese
alessandro-farnese-cardinal.summary: An Italian cardinal, diplomat and major art patron (1520-1589), grandson of Pope Paul III and son of Pier Luigi Farnese, Duke of Parma, who was murdered in 1547.

michael-friedrich-von-althann.name: Michael Friedrich von Althann
michael-friedrich-von-althann.summary: A Holy Roman clergyman and politician (1680–1734), bishop of Vác, who served as viceroy of the Kingdom of Naples and Sicily.

roman-inquisition.name: Roman Inquisition
roman-inquisition.summary: Catholic Church tribunal established in 1542 by Pope Paul III to prosecute people over religious or doctrinal offenses, one of three branches alongside the Spanish and Portuguese Inquisitions.

geocentrism.name: Aristotelian Cosmology
geocentrism.summary: An outdated model placing Earth at the center of the universe, with the Sun, Moon, and planets orbiting it, dominant from ancient Greece through the medieval period.

franciscus-patricius.name: Franciscus Patricius
franciscus-patricius.summary: Philosopher and scientist (1529–1597) from Cres in the Republic of Venice, a defender of Platonism who became a sharp, high-profile opponent of Aristotelianism.

cres.name: Cres
cres.summary: An Adriatic island in Croatia's Kvarner Gulf, about 406 square kilometres in area, once joined to the neighbouring island of Lošinj before the two were separated by a channel.

platonism.name: Platonism
platonism.summary: The philosophy of Plato and its derivatives, holding that abstract Forms exist in a realm distinct from the physical and mental worlds, deeply influencing later Western thought.

aristotelianism.name: Aristotelianism
aristotelianism.summary: A philosophical tradition based on Aristotle's work, marked by deductive logic and the study of natural philosophy, later carried forward by Islamic Golden Age scholars.

federico-cesi.name: Federico Cesi
federico-cesi.summary: An Italian scientist and naturalist (1585–1630) who founded the Accademia dei Lincei and later briefly became lord of Acquasparta.

accademia-dei-lincei.name: Accademia dei Lincei
accademia-dei-lincei.summary: An Italian scientific academy active from 1603 to 1651, founded in Rome by Federico Cesi, with Galileo Galilei as its intellectual centre.

university-of-padua.name: University of Padua
university-of-padua.summary: Founded in 1222 by scholars from Bologna, one of early modern Europe's leading universities, known for rigorous Aristotelian science and figures like Galileo and Vesalius.

university-of-ferrara.name: University of Ferrara
university-of-ferrara.summary: The main university of Ferrara in northern Italy, once the best-attended of Italy's free universities before World War I.

pope-gregory-xiv.name: Pope Gregory XIV
pope-gregory-xiv.summary: Born Niccolò Sfondrato, head of the Catholic Church from December 1590 until his death in October 1591.

pierre-gassendi.name: Pierre Gassendi
pierre-gassendi.summary: French philosopher, priest, astronomer and mathematician (1592–1655) who tracked the 1631 transit of Mercury and tried to reconcile Epicurean atomism with Christianity.

pierre-bayle.name: Pierre Bayle
pierre-bayle.summary: French philosopher and lexicographer (1647–1706), author of the Historical and Critical Dictionary; his skepticism and advocacy of religious toleration influenced the Enlightenment.

gian-lorenzo-bernini.name: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
gian-lorenzo-bernini.summary: Italian sculptor, architect and painter (1598 to 1680) credited with creating Baroque sculpture and regarded as the leading sculptor of his age.

pope-alexander-vii.name: Pope Alexander VII
pope-alexander-vii.summary: Born Fabio Chigi, head of the Catholic Church from 1655 to 1667; interested in architecture, he patronized artists and urban projects in Rome.

val-camonica-witch-trials.name: Val Camonica witch trials
val-camonica-witch-trials.summary: Two large witch trials held in Val Camonica, Italy, in 1505-1510 and 1518-1521, whose records were later destroyed on the bishop of Brescia's orders.

giacinto-gaggia.name: Giacinto Gaggia
giacinto-gaggia.summary: Italian Roman Catholic bishop of Brescia from 1913 until his death in 1933, made an archbishop in 1930.
